correctness.rationale: Hermite divisibility and Euler-jet equivalence give exact constraints. Minimum-norm finite Gram solution is exact; scaled matrix entries converge to a block-diagonal direct sum of positive Hilbert moment matrices at O(1/K), including off-diagonal oscillatory estimates. Inversion yields the O(K^-2) norm remainder and a uniform O(K^-1) coefficient remainder. The Hilbert inverse first column is the shifted Legendre evaluation kernel, with zeroth entry m². Exact polynomial identities and independently constructed numerical Gram checks corroborate but are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This fills the explicit mixed-multiplicity boundary-zero gap named in the primary article, gives the sharp degree-to-error law and a uniform coefficient-level limit for the entire least-squares inverse filter. Quadratic multiplicity contributions differ materially from simple-root counting, and their Legendre structure identifies universal local profile shapes relevant to boundary-sensitive optimal Hardy approximation. Fixed-node assumptions and absence of collision-uniform estimates are clearly delimited.
